svg.title: How money moves through the trust account

g.text: Every entry is one of four kinds; its circled number is the step that made it
Cash · money in the trust account
Clearing · in and out, back to $0
Outside AA: the payers who pay in, and the anaesthetists' own bank accounts
Holds each procedure and raises its invoice first, then
submits it to Xero. Its ledger mirrors Xero, and must equal it.
AA's trust accounting. Debits on the left, credits
on the right. A receivable is an invoice here, and
AA's one real bank account. Every receipt lands
here; every payout and refund leaves from here.
A current asset. Every invoice and its bill post through it,
so it reads $0; money left in it means the two are out of step.
Accounts receivable: the invoices. A control
account: only the total owed to AA.
Accounts payable: the bills. A control account:
The bill to the anaesthetist is expected to be the
buyer-created tax invoice. Whether there is one per
procedure or one per payment run is still open (OQ-29).
A creditor beside the anaesthetists, "a fake anaesthetist": it
receives and transfers, but is never paid itself. Not a bank
account and not a ledger account. One for all prepayments;
money leaves it only through the system.
Clearing reads $0, each sub-ledger equals its control
account, our ledger equals Xero, and no bank lines are
left unmatched. If not, the payment run stops.
A posted bill is an approved bill
In Xero, the bill to Dr Nick could be paid before Patient 1 pays.
Our ledger releases it only once Patient 1 has paid; how Xero is
kept from paying it early is still open. The catalogue holds the
bill as a draft until then (US-09.1.1), which would not post to Clearing.
Prepayment invoice approved in our system
The whiteboard drew this bill when the money comes in. This
drawing posts it with the invoice, so Clearing stays at $0, as
the catalogue has it (OQ-80). Still to confirm with Greg and Sam.
A move between two creditors, not a payment or a new invoice;
no cash moves. How Xero posts it is still open, and so is what
releases it once the procedure is done (OQ-125).
The payment cycle and its day are still to confirm (OQ-47);
The bulk payment add-on makes a BNZ file; a director
approves it, not whoever reconciled the bank.

svg.text: Every dollar in the trust account is owed to someone: Clearing reads $0, each sub-ledger equals its control account, and our ledger equals Xero
